correctness.rationale: For n≥2 there is no dominating singleton; in a matching a set dominates exactly when it hits every edge, and the perfect-coalition neighbor restrictions are automatic. Form the support Q of endpoint-class types. The partner edges are exactly the two-element covers of Q, and every class must occur in one. A loop forces all partner edges through its class and an edge avoiding that class then gives at most three classes. In the loopless case a family of edges with no common vertex either contains disjoint edges, bounding all participating labels by four, or contains a triangle, bounding them by three. With four labels Q must be 2K₂, P₄, or C₄; the other supports containing two disjoint edges have isolated partner vertices. Taking two-element covers gives respectively C₄, P₄, and 2K₂. Surjections of labeled edges onto the support, independent endpoint orientations, and division by the 4! free class namings give the three formulas, including n=2 and n=3. Two disjoint types used at least once attain four for all n≥2.
residual_risks: The replay checks only four finite sizes; the support argument provides the unrestricted proof.
